definition: The equation linking the pressure, volume, amount and temperature of an ideal gas: $PV = nRT$, or $PV = Nk_\text{B}T$ when counting molecules. The temperature must be in kelvin.
The constant $R$ in $PV = nRT$, the same for every ideal gas: $R = \pu{8.31 J mol-1 K-1}$. It equals the Avogadro constant multiplied by the Boltzmann constant, $R = N_\text{A}k_\text{B}$.
The square root of the mean of the squares of the speeds of the molecules in a gas, $v_\text{rms} = \sqrt{\overline{v^{2}}}$. Its square is the $v^{2}$ in $P = \frac{1}{3}\rho v^{2}$.
